title: ABM pilot kickoff - regulated verticals (finserv + healthcare)
summary: Internal kickoff for the 6–8 week vertical ABM pilot targeting regulated workloads. Team aligned on primary goals (validate repeatable positioning + outbound motion, ship durable vertical assets, generate qualified pipeline for Dedicated/Private). Discussed whether to start with financial services only vs running finserv + healthcare in parallel; decision: prioritize finserv for weeks 1–4, keep healthcare assets in draft and pull forward if bandwidth allows / if we get warm signals. Reviewed asset plan (landing page, one-pagers, security FAQ + evidence pack index, outbound sequences, deck/battlecard, webinar outline, metrics dashboard), named owners, and set weekly cadence. Flagged key risks: compliance-safe claims (avoid “HIPAA-ready”), security questionnaire turnaround time, limited vertical proof points/logos, and inconsistent packaging guidance between Dedicated vs Private. Closed with concrete next steps and review gates for external copy.
topics: Pilot goals and success criteria (meetings, SQLs, POCs, conversion to procurement)
Vertical selection: financial services vs healthcare (or both)
Messaging guardrails for regulated claims (SOC 2, encryption, audit logs, SSO/SAML, retention/residency)
Asset list and owners (landing page, one-pagers, security FAQ, evidence pack, sequences, deck, webinar)
Target account list, scoring, and assignment to NA/EMEA
Measurement plan and attribution (UTMs, HubSpot stages, outreach tracking)
Risks and dependencies (security bandwidth, proof points, packaging/pricing consistency)

transcript:
Meeting: ABM pilot kickoff — regulated verticals (finserv + healthcare)
Recorded by Fireflies
Date: 2025-05-02
Start time: 10:03 AM PT
Duration: 54 min

Attendees:
- Camila Reyes (VP Marketing)
- Ben Carter (Growth Marketing)
- Soojin Lee (Product Marketing)
- Ethan Wallace (Content)
- Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)
- Grace O'Connor (SDR Programs)
- Stephanie Nguyen (NA Sales)
- Lukas Meyer (EMEA Sales)
- Markus Klein (Solutions Engineering)
- Naomi Feldman (Security/Compliance)
- Dr. Aisha Rahman (Security)
- Vivek Kulkarni (Product, Private Deployments)
- Lauren Bishop (Product, Dedicated)
- Elliot Price (Docs)


[10:03:12] Ben Carter: Cool, I think we’re good to start. This is the kickoff for the regulated workloads ABM pilot. Fireflies is on. Um, goal today is alignment on vertical choice, asset plan, owners, and timeline, and we’ll call out risks early so we’re not surprised week three.

[10:03:36] Camila Reyes: Yep. And also, just to frame it, we’re not building a bunch of new product features for this. This is a go-to-market validation exercise. So small docs updates, packaging clarification, enablement, yes. Net-new roadmap items, no, unless they’re tiny.

[10:03:57] Soojin Lee: Plus we have to be really careful on claims. Regulated audiences are allergic to hand-wavy “trust us” language.

[10:04:09] Ben Carter: Exactly. Okay. I’ll start with what success looks like. We have a 6 to 8 week pilot. Success is not page views. It’s: meetings booked with the right personas, SQLs created, and ideally one to two POCs kicked off that convert into procurement motion for Dedicated and/or Private.

[10:04:33] Tyler Benson: And we’ll define what counts as a meeting, too. Like, not a 15 minute “nice to meet you.” We want at least one of: technical discovery, security review, or pilot scoping.

[10:04:45] Ben Carter: Yep. Personas we’re going after: CISO / Security leadership, Platform or ML engineering, and Procurement or vendor management.

[10:04:58] Stephanie Nguyen: From sales side, I want to make sure we’re not blasting generic “LLM infra” messaging. If it’s regulated, they’re going to ask audit logs, SSO, KMS, retention like, in the first five minutes.

[10:05:12] Naomi Feldman: They will. And they’ll ask for SOC 2 on email one.

[10:05:16] Ben Carter: Great segue. Let’s talk verticals. We had two candidates: financial services and healthcare. The question is do we do one, or do we do both.

[10:05:29] Camila Reyes: I’m leaning one to start. Our bandwidth is not infinite and the compliance review loop will slow us down if we try to ship two full sets of assets.

[10:05:42] Lukas Meyer: In EMEA, I’ll add: healthcare messaging gets weird fast. Not just HIPAA obviously, but data residency, GDPR, retention requirements, and then you get into “is this medical device software” type conversations. It can spiral.

[10:05:59] Grace O'Connor: On the outbound side, job title targeting is already narrow. If we split across verticals we might end up with low volume audiences and not learn anything.

[10:06:10] Soojin Lee: Counterpoint: healthcare is where the “PHI-adjacent” language could resonate, and it’s a good forcing function to tighten our claim language. But I agree we should not promise “HIPAA-ready” or “HIPAA compliant” in ads. That phrase is a trap.

[10:06:28] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. Please, no “HIPAA-ready.” If we use anything, it has to be like “supports deployment patterns and controls commonly required for regulated workloads” and then enumerate controls. And even then we need to footnote what’s in-scope.

[10:06:46] Ben Carter: So maybe an approach: we prioritize finserv in weeks one through four, ship finserv assets, and keep healthcare in draft, ready to accelerate if we get warm signals or if we have bandwidth.

[10:07:00] Ethan Wallace: That helps content. We can write the landing page to be “regulated workloads” generic, then have vertical forks: finserv one-pager and healthcare one-pager. But only one of those gets finished in week two.

[10:07:16] Camila Reyes: That’s basically my vote.

[10:07:20] Stephanie Nguyen: Same. Finserv first. We already have a few named targets that are asking VPC and audit log stuff. It’s the cleanest to learn.

[10:07:30] Lukas Meyer: Agree.

[10:07:31] Ben Carter: Okay, decision recorded: finserv is the primary for the pilot, healthcare is secondary / optional depending on bandwidth and response.

[10:07:42] Tyler Benson: We should write that into the KPI doc so nobody is confused. Like, “go/no-go on healthcare assets” at end of week two.

[10:07:51] Ben Carter: Yup.

[10:07:54] Ben Carter: Asset plan. I’m going to rattle off the list and we’ll assign owners.

[10:08:00] Ben Carter: One: regulated workloads landing page. Two: finserv one-pager (focus on Private + Dedicated). Three: security FAQ — sales-ready. Four: evidence pack index and sharing process. Five: outbound sequences (email + LinkedIn). Six: enablement deck + battlecard. Seven: webinar outline, optional. Eight: metrics dashboard spec.

[10:08:26] Elliot Price: For the landing page, we should keep it extremely simple: “deployment options,” “controls,” “operational tooling,” then CTA. If the copy turns into a whitepaper nobody will read it.

[10:08:36] Soojin Lee: Messaging wise the pillars should be: deployment flexibility (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), operational evidence (audit logs, access controls, retention), and performance economics (predictable throughput, cost controls, graceful degradation). But we have to tie it to outcomes: “reduce time-to-approval” and “lower cost per analyzed case” etc.

[10:08:58] Markus Klein: And we should include a ‘pilot plan’ CTA. Like, “two-week benchmark + architecture validation.” Because otherwise the conversation stalls at “send me a datasheet.”

[10:09:09] Ben Carter: Great. Owners: Ethan, can you own landing page copy and the finserv one-pager draft?

[10:09:16] Ethan Wallace: Yes. I’ll need final claim guardrails from Soojin and sign-off from Naomi/Aisha before anything goes external.

[10:09:25] Ben Carter: That’s fair. Soojin owns messaging framework and approved language.

[10:09:30] Soojin Lee: Yup. I’ll put together an “approved language” doc and a “do not say” list. We’ll include examples: “HIPAA-ready” is no, “SOC2 certified” is no, “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” is yes.

[10:09:46] Naomi Feldman: Thank you. Also “we never store customer data” — careful. We need to define what that means for logs, telemetry, retention settings. We can say “configurable retention” and “no training on customer data” with the right qualifiers.

[10:10:02] Dr. Aisha Rahman: And “air-gapped” should be reserved. Unless we truly have that packaging ready.

[10:10:07] Vivek Kulkarni: We have an on-prem option but “air-gapped” depends on the customer environment. So we should say “on-prem / isolated network deployment options” and keep it precise.

[10:10:18] Ben Carter: Great. Naomi and Aisha, can you own the security FAQ language and the evidence pack index? Or at least final approval.

[10:10:26] Naomi Feldman: I can own coordination. Daniel is not on this call, but he’s been helping with evidence packaging. We’ll keep it to an index and a request process. We are not sending SOC2 on a public link.

[10:10:40] Dr. Aisha Rahman: And we should define the “security review fast path.” Like, what we can answer via FAQ versus what triggers a questionnaire.

[10:10:49] Markus Klein: Yes, because SEs get pulled into 20-page spreadsheets and it kills response time.

[10:10:55] Ben Carter: Okay. Markus, can you draft that fast path checklist plus the pilot plan template?

[10:11:02] Markus Klein: Yes. I’ll draft discovery questions too.

[10:11:06] Ben Carter: Grace, outbound sequences and coordination with AEs?

[10:11:10] Grace O'Connor: Yes. We’ll do a 3 to 5 touch sequence. First email is security-oriented CTA: “Want the evidence pack index?” Second is performance economics. Third is “pilot plan.” LinkedIn touches mirror it.

[10:11:28] Stephanie Nguyen: One thing: don’t lead with “download our PDF.” Lead with “15-minute security fit check” or “we’ll map your requirements to deployment mode.” People will ignore PDFs.

[10:11:39] Grace O'Connor: Totally. The PDF is support, not the ask.

[10:11:43] Ben Carter: Tyler, metrics + attribution?

[10:11:46] Tyler Benson: Yep. I’ll set up UTM conventions and define the dashboard: target coverage, touches sent, replies, meetings, SQLs, POC starts, stage velocity.

[10:11:58] Ben Carter: Perfect.

[10:12:01] Ben Carter: Now timeline. Weeks one and two are prep. That’s: accounts, messaging, assets, measurement. Weeks three through six execution. Weeks seven and eight: close and write-up.

[10:12:14] Camila Reyes: And weekly cadence: 30 minute standup with owners. Plus a separate security content review slot so we’re not doing approvals in Slack at midnight.

[10:12:24] Naomi Feldman: Please.

[10:12:26] Ben Carter: I’ll send recurring invite after this.

[10:12:30] Ben Carter: Let’s talk target account list quickly. Stephanie, are we comfortable with the current finserv list? We’ll finalize in a separate doc review but high level.

[10:12:39] Stephanie Nguyen: High level yes. We have a mix: banks, insurance, payments, wealth. I’d bias toward teams that already have a GenAI initiative and are hitting compliance walls. And teams looking at moving off AWS Bedrock or Azure OpenAI for cost predictability or data isolation.

[10:12:57] Lukas Meyer: For EMEA: add more “payments” and “neo-banks.” Traditional banks have longer cycles. The pilot is eight weeks; we need deals that can move.

[10:13:09] Ben Carter: Good point. We’ll include faster-cycle accounts.

[10:13:13] Soojin Lee: Messaging per sub-vertical might differ. Insurance is very audit-heavy. Payments are latency heavy. Wealth is SSO and governance heavy. We should not force one talk track.

[10:13:28] Ben Carter: Right. That’s why we’ll have persona matrix rather than a single paragraph.

[10:13:33] Elliot Price: Also, please do not put “SOC2” and “ISO” logos on the landing page if we don’t have the permission. We can say “SOC 2 Type II available under NDA.”

[10:13:43] Naomi Feldman: Correct. And we need to confirm ISO status and scope. If we’re mid-audit we can’t imply completion.

[10:13:52] Dr. Aisha Rahman: This is where people over-claim and we pay for it in questionnaires later.

[10:13:58] Ben Carter: Okay, risk log time. I’ve got three already: (1) compliance-safe language, (2) security questionnaire bandwidth/turnaround, (3) proof points.

[10:14:09] Ethan Wallace: On proof points: do we have any regulated customer story we can use, even anonymized? Like “top-10 bank” or “large payer” type.

[10:14:18] Camila Reyes: We can do genericized proof points, but we need internal approval. No customer names without explicit permission.

[10:14:26] Stephanie Nguyen: Sales can provide “anonymized pattern” statements: “regional bank running call summarization” etc. But we should be careful about specificity.

[10:14:36] Markus Klein: For credibility, we can use benchmark numbers and architecture diagrams. Those are safer.

[10:14:43] Soojin Lee: Yes, but benchmark claims also need context. “Up to X tokens per second” needs hardware + model details. Otherwise it becomes marketing fluff.

[10:14:54] Vivek Kulkarni: Another risk: packaging confusion. Prospects ask “Dedicated vs Private.” We need crisp decision tree: data boundary, networking, who manages the cluster, residency, and SLA.

[10:15:09] Lauren Bishop: I can provide a simple mapping. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our environment with isolation controls; Private is customer-controlled networking (VPC/on-prem). We need to align on how we talk about data handling and what security controls exist in each.

[10:15:26] Naomi Feldman: Plus what audit logs exist in each mode and where logs go.

[10:15:31] Tyler Benson: From measurement standpoint, another risk: low volume. Especially if LinkedIn targeting is too narrow. We should define a minimum sample size and backup channels like partner co-sell.

[10:15:45] Ben Carter: Good. Add risk: low-volume audience + channel.

[10:15:49] Grace O'Connor: And deliverability. If we send from too many new inboxes at once we’ll hit spam. We should phase outreach.

[10:15:56] Ben Carter: Add risk: deliverability.

[10:15:59] Camila Reyes: Another one: security review response time. If we can’t respond in 48 hours we lose momentum. We need a triage process.

[10:16:09] Naomi Feldman: Agree. We can template responses for the top 20 questions. Olga can help but she’s not here.

[10:16:16] Dr. Aisha Rahman: And we should define what we will not answer without an NDA or without a security review call. Example: full SOC report, pen test details.

[10:16:26] Ben Carter: Great.

[10:16:28] Ben Carter: Let’s do a quick pass on the landing page CTA. There was debate: “book a security review” vs “download benchmark” vs “request evidence pack.”

[10:16:39] Soojin Lee: For regulated, I like “request security pack” or “book a 20-minute security fit check.” A benchmark download is more engineering. Security buyers won’t click it.

[10:16:52] Stephanie Nguyen: +1. And it’s a good qualifier. People who ask for the pack are real.

[10:16:57] Markus Klein: I’d add a secondary CTA for engineers: “See reference architecture.” But keep primary CTA security/fit check.

[10:17:06] Elliot Price: We also need to ensure whatever we link is not gated behind some random Google Drive share. It should be in docs with appropriate gating.

[10:17:16] Ben Carter: Understood. The evidence pack will be an index page, and then “request access” for restricted artifacts.

[10:17:25] Naomi Feldman: Exactly.

[10:17:28] Ben Carter: Okay, last piece: weekly governance. I propose:
- Weekly 30 min pilot standup (owners)
- Weekly 30 min security + messaging review (Soojin, Naomi, Aisha, Ethan)
- Biweekly pipeline review with Stephanie/Lukas

[10:17:47] Lukas Meyer: Works.

[10:17:49] Stephanie Nguyen: Works.

[10:17:51] Camila Reyes: Works, and I want a short written update each week: what shipped, what’s blocked, top learnings.

[10:18:00] Ben Carter: Okay.

[10:18:03] Ben Carter: Open questions before we close?

[10:18:06] Speaker 1: Sorry, quick one — are we doing healthcare at all in this first month?

[10:18:12] Ben Carter: Not unless we hit a go/no-go at end of week two and feel good on bandwidth. We’ll keep a draft in motion so we’re not starting from zero.

[10:18:23] Soojin Lee: Also, let’s be careful: healthcare language has legal review implications. If we touch PHI explicitly, it can trigger a different level of scrutiny.

[10:18:33] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yep.

[10:18:35] Ethan Wallace: I’ll write healthcare content as “PHI-adjacent / sensitive data workloads” and keep it in draft until we decide.

[10:18:44] Ben Carter: Great.

[10:18:46] Ben Carter: Quick recap of owners:
- Pilot lead: Ben
- Exec sponsor: Camila
- Messaging/claims: Soojin
- Landing page + finserv one-pager: Ethan (with Elliot on docs process)
- Security FAQ + evidence pack index: Naomi/Aisha
- Sequences: Grace
- Metrics: Tyler
- SE pilot plan + fast path: Markus
- Product mapping Dedicated/Private: Vivek + Lauren

[10:19:16] Ben Carter: I’ll send notes and the action items today.

[10:19:20] Camila Reyes: And please put a hard gate on external copy: Security must review before anything is published or used in outbound.

[10:19:28] Ben Carter: Will do.

[10:19:30] Naomi Feldman: One more: if anyone is asked about audit log fields, don’t improvise. We’ll provide exact wording and sample fields we can stand behind.

[10:19:39] Markus Klein: Thank you.

[10:19:41] Ben Carter: Alright, thanks everyone. We’ll reconvene next week with drafts and the account list.

[10:19:47] Meeting ended
